summary: Warehouse timeouts correlated with unit economics backfill job (hourly aggregates) saturating compute
description:
Issue summary:
- Beginning ~09:10 PT 2025-02-19, multiple internal Console pages (Unit Economics dashboard + a few ad-hoc analytics views) began timing out.
- Warehouse query latency and queueing spiked; several scheduled transforms missed their window.

Impact:
- Internal users (Finance/Product/Eng) saw intermittent 30–60s timeouts when loading Unit Economics dashboard drilldowns.
- Other warehouse-backed services experienced elevated p95 query latency (not a full outage).
- Risk: data freshness SLO breaches if scheduled jobs continue to miss hourly completion.

Detection:
- #eng-platform reported “Unit Econ drilldowns spinning / timing out.”
- Observability: warehouse concurrency/queue depth increased; high warehouse credit consumption.

Suspected cause:
- Unit economics historical backfill job (2025Q1) running with too-high parallelism and competing with interactive queries and scheduled materializations.
- The backfill appears to be triggering large scans against raw metering tables and re-materializing hourly aggregates repeatedly (idempotency is correct, but chunking is too coarse).

What we need:
1) Immediate mitigation to reduce warehouse contention (throttle / schedule backfill in off-hours / isolate compute).
2) Confirm no data corruption (partial writes / duplicate hours).
3) Follow-up tasks for sustainable backfill strategy (resource isolation, smaller partitions, guardrails).

Notes:
- Backfill tooling introduced in PR-19412; warehouse view optimizations in PR-19405 may help but are not fully deployed everywhere.
- This is internal-only; no customer-facing incident declared.
comments: 2025-02-19 09:24 PT — Allison Grant (reporter): Seeing elevated timeouts across warehouse-backed endpoints. Unit Econ dashboard top-N tables fail ~50% of the time. Can someone confirm if a backfill is running? Any chance we can pause it until we isolate impact?

2025-02-19 09:31 PT — Mei Lin (assignee): Confirmed: unit economics 2025Q1 backfill kicked off at 08:55 PT using new backfill tooling (PR-19412). It’s running with concurrency=24 and hour-range chunks of 72h. Warehouse queue depth is climbing. I can pause the job now and rerun with lower concurrency + smaller chunks.

2025-02-19 09:36 PT — Sean Gallagher: +1 to pausing. We’re also seeing other scheduled jobs slipping. Recommendation: throttle backfill to single-digit concurrency and run in maintenance window (evenings PT). Longer-term: isolate to a separate warehouse/compute pool if possible.

2025-02-19 09:41 PT — Mei Lin: Paused backfill run (job id: ue_backfill_2025q1_0219_0855). Queue depth already dropping. Next: re-run with concurrency=6, chunk_size=6h, and explicit sleep between chunks (30s) to yield capacity.
2025-02-19 10:03 PT — Chloe Martin: Console team confirming dashboards recover as soon as warehouse queue clears. Please keep us posted on a safe throttle so we can unblock Finance dogfood today.

2025-02-19 10:12 PT — Mei Lin: Re-ran backfill with concurrency=6 and smaller chunks. Warehouse load is steady; interactive queries p95 back to normal. Credits/hr still elevated but within expected tolerance. Will keep monitoring for the next ~2 hours before leaving it unattended.

2025-02-19 10:28 PT — Caleb Johnson: Data quality check: no duplicate hours detected in the hourly aggregate table for the affected window. Completeness is slightly behind while job was paused, but should recover. Please ensure the job writes are idempotent by partition (hour, model, region, tier).

2025-02-19 11:05 PT — Mei Lin: Confirmed idempotent upserts by hour partition. Also adding a guardrail: cap max concurrency to 8 in the backfill runner config so we don’t repeat this. I’ll open follow-ups for (1) compute isolation and (2) further query optimization.

2025-02-19 11:22 PT — Allison Grant: Marking incident mitigated. Please document recommended backfill parameters in the oncall guide and link it here. Also: we should add an alert on warehouse queue depth correlated with backfill tag if possible.

2025-02-20 09:14 PT — Mei Lin: Update: Backfill ran overnight (18:00–06:00 PT) at concurrency=6 without impacting daytime traffic. Added a runbook note (draft) on throttle + scheduling. Remaining work is tracking items below.

2025-02-21 16:40 PT — Sean Gallagher: Closing out since mitigation is stable. Follow-ups are captured. SRE ask: default backfill schedule should avoid business hours and require an explicit acknowledgement in #eng-oncall when starting large runs.
resolution: Paused high-concurrency backfill run; re-ran with throttled concurrency and smaller chunk sizes + inter-chunk sleep. Scheduled subsequent backfill to off-hours to prevent contention. Verified no duplicate/partial-hour corruption in aggregates.
workaround: If dashboards or scheduled jobs time out during backfill: pause the backfill runner, reduce concurrency (<=6), reduce chunk size (<=6h), and run outside 08:00–18:00 PT. Prefer running on isolated compute if available.
follow_up_tasks: Create a dedicated/isolated warehouse (or separate compute pool) for backfills so interactive queries aren’t contended (owner: Sean Gallagher).
Add a hard-coded max concurrency guardrail in the backfill runner and require an override flag + oncall acknowledgement for higher values (owner: Mei Lin).
Improve partition pruning / materialized view strategy for raw metering scans used by backfill (owner: Mei Lin; aligns with ENG-8431 / PR-19405).
Add alerting for warehouse queue depth + long-running backfill queries tagged `unit_econ_backfill` (owner: Aisha Bello).
Update oncall guide with recommended backfill parameters and verification queries (owner: Caleb Johnson).
